name: Edward Burnett Tylor
summary: British classical evolutionist who gave the classic definition of culture and proposed animism as the earliest form of religion.
note: Not Stephen Tyler, the cognitive anthropologist.

name: James George Frazer
summary: British classical evolutionist who traced a sequence from magic through religion to science.

name: Lewis Henry Morgan
summary: American classical evolutionist who studied the Iroquois, founded kinship studies and set out stages of savagery, barbarism and civilisation.

name: John Ferguson McLennan
summary: Scottish evolutionist who coined exogamy and endogamy and argued that early marriage was by capture.

name: Franz Boas
summary: German-born founder of American anthropology who rejected unilinear evolution and stressed each culture's particular history and cultural relativism.

name: Alfred Louis Kroeber
summary: Boas's student who treated culture as superorganic and mapped the culture areas of native North America.

name: Clark Wissler
summary: American diffusionist who developed the culture area and age-area concepts from American Indian data.

name: Ruth Benedict
summary: Culture-and-personality pioneer who saw each culture as an integrated configuration, like a personality writ large.

name: Margaret Mead
summary: Benedict's student whose Samoa and New Guinea studies argued that adolescence and sex roles are shaped by culture.
note: Not George Herbert Mead, the sociologist.

name: Ralph Linton
summary: American anthropologist who defined status and role and worked with Kardiner on basic personality structure.

name: Abram Kardiner
summary: American psychoanalyst who, with Linton, held that primary institutions such as child-rearing form a society's basic personality structure.

name: Cora Du Bois
summary: American anthropologist whose fieldwork on Alor in Indonesia produced the concept of modal personality.
note: Not W.E.B. Du Bois.

name: Bronisław Malinowski
summary: Polish-born British anthropologist who founded functionalism and modern participant-observation fieldwork in the Trobriand Islands.

name: A.R. Radcliffe-Brown
summary: British founder of structural-functionalism, who studied how institutions maintain social structure; did fieldwork in the Andaman Islands.

name: E.E. Evans-Pritchard
summary: British social anthropologist known for his studies of Azande witchcraft and the stateless, segmentary Nuer.

name: Edmund Leach
summary: British anthropologist who showed Kachin politics swinging between gumsa and gumlao forms and brought structuralism into British anthropology.

name: Claude Lévi-Strauss
summary: French founder of structural anthropology, who read kinship, myth and classification as products of universal binary structures of the mind.

name: Victor Turner
summary: British symbolic anthropologist who studied Ndembu ritual and developed the ideas of liminality and communitas.

name: Arnold van Gennep
summary: French ethnographer and folklorist who identified the three-phase structure of rites of passage.

name: Clifford Geertz
summary: American interpretive anthropologist who treated culture as public webs of meaning to be read through thick description.

name: David M. Schneider
summary: American symbolic anthropologist who studied kinship as a cultural system of symbols and meanings.

name: Stephen A. Tyler
summary: American cognitive anthropologist who edited Cognitive Anthropology (1969) and later wrote on post-modern ethnography.
note: Not E.B. Tylor, the classical evolutionist.

name: Harold C. Conklin
summary: American ethnoscientist who studied Hanunóo colour categories and swidden farming in the Philippines through the people's own classifications.

name: Mary Douglas
summary: British anthropologist who treated pollution as a matter of classification, with dirt as matter out of place, and devised grid-group analysis.

name: Leslie A. White
summary: American neo-evolutionist who tied cultural evolution to the energy harnessed per person (universal evolution).

name: Julian Steward
summary: American neo-evolutionist who proposed multilinear evolution and founded cultural ecology.

name: Marshall Sahlins
summary: American anthropologist who, with Service, separated general and specific evolution, and classified reciprocity in Stone Age Economics.

name: Elman Service
summary: American neo-evolutionist who classified political organisation into band, tribe, chiefdom and state.

name: V. Gordon Childe
summary: Australian-born prehistorian and neo-evolutionist who named the Neolithic and Urban Revolutions.

name: Marvin Harris
summary: American founder of cultural materialism, which explains culture by its techno-economic and demographic infrastructure.

name: Karl Polanyi
summary: Hungarian economic historian whose substantivist approach classed economies by reciprocity, redistribution and market exchange.

name: Marcel Mauss
summary: French sociologist and Durkheim's nephew who analysed the gift as a total social fact binding giver and receiver.

name: Émile Durkheim
summary: French sociologist who defined religion by the sacred and studied Australian totemism as its elementary form.

name: R.R. Marett
summary: British anthropologist who proposed animatism, belief in an impersonal supernatural power, as a stage before animism.

name: Max Müller
aliases: Max Muller|Friedrich Max Müller|F. Max Müller
summary: German-born Oxford philologist and Indologist who explained the origin of religion as naturism, the personification of nature.

name: Grafton Elliot Smith
summary: Australian-born anatomist and British diffusionist who, with W.J. Perry, derived all civilisation from ancient Egypt.

name: W.H.R. Rivers
summary: British anthropologist and psychologist who devised the genealogical method, studied the Todas and later turned to diffusionism.

name: Edward Sapir
summary: American linguist-anthropologist and student of Boas whose view that language shapes thought underlies the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis.

name: Fredrik Barth
summary: Norwegian anthropologist who defined ethnic groups by the boundaries they maintain rather than by their cultural content.

name: Charles Darwin
summary: English naturalist who proposed evolution by natural selection.

name: Gregor Mendel
summary: Augustinian friar of Brünn (Brno) whose pea-plant experiments gave the laws of segregation and independent assortment.

name: Thomas Robert Malthus
summary: English economist who argued that population grows geometrically while food supply grows only arithmetically.

name: Herbert Hope Risley
summary: British administrator and Census Commissioner for 1901 who classified India's people into seven racial types and gave a racial theory of caste.

name: J.H. Hutton
summary: British administrator-ethnographer of the Nagas and Census Commissioner for 1931, who wrote Caste in India.

name: Sarat Chandra Roy
summary: Ranchi lawyer and pioneer Indian ethnographer of the Munda, Oraon and other Chotanagpur tribes, who founded the journal Man in India.

name: B.S. Guha
summary: Indian physical anthropologist who classified India's population into six main racial elements and was the first director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

name: Verrier Elwin
summary: British-born ethnographer of central Indian tribes who first argued for shielding them from outsiders, then advised Nehru on tribal policy in NEFA.

name: G.S. Ghurye
summary: Indian sociologist who set out six features of caste and called tribes backward Hindus, arguing for their assimilation.

name: D.N. Majumdar
summary: Lucknow anthropologist who studied the Ho and other tribes, race and caste in India, and village communities.

name: Nirmal Kumar Bose
summary: Indian anthropologist who described the Hindu method of tribal absorption and the structure of Hindu society.

name: Irawati Karve
summary: Indian anthropologist who mapped Indian kinship into northern, central, southern and eastern zones.

name: L.P. Vidyarthi
summary: Ranchi anthropologist who formulated the sacred complex and the Nature-Man-Spirit complex and traced the phases of Indian anthropology.

name: S.C. Dube
summary: Indian anthropologist whose study of Shamirpet near Hyderabad was among the first full Indian village monographs.

name: M.N. Srinivas
summary: Indian social anthropologist who formulated Sanskritisation, Westernisation and dominant caste, and studied the village of Rampura.

name: Robert Redfield
summary: American anthropologist of peasant society who proposed the folk-urban continuum and the great and little traditions.

name: McKim Marriott
summary: American anthropologist whose study of Kishan Garhi village described universalisation and parochialisation.

name: Louis Dumont
summary: French anthropologist who explained caste as hierarchy built on the opposition of the pure and the impure.

name: F.G. Bailey
summary: British anthropologist of highland Odisha who proposed the tribe-caste continuum.

name: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf
summary: Austrian-born anthropologist of the tribes of Hyderabad and North-East India who advised on tribal welfare.

name: Primitive Culture
summary: Opens with Tylor's definition of culture as a complex whole and sets out animism and survivals in an evolutionary account of religion.

name: The Golden Bough
aliases: Golden Bough|The Golden Bough: A Study in Magic and Religion
summary: Comparative study of magic and religion proposing an evolutionary sequence from magic to religion to science.
note: First published in two volumes in 1890; later enlarged to twelve volumes.

name: Ancient Society
summary: Traces human progress through savagery, barbarism and civilisation, linked to inventions, forms of family, government and property.

name: The Mind of Primitive Man
summary: Argues that race, language and culture vary independently and that no race is innately inferior in mental capacity.

name: Patterns of Culture
summary: Compares the Zuni, Dobu and Kwakiutl as integrated configurations, calling the Zuni Apollonian and the Kwakiutl Dionysian.
note: Benedict took the Apollonian-Dionysian contrast from Nietzsche.

name: Coming of Age in Samoa
summary: Argues that Samoan girls pass through adolescence without Western stress, so adolescent turmoil is cultural rather than biological.
note: Challenged by Derek Freeman in 1983.

name: Argonauts of the Western Pacific
summary: Trobriand ethnography of the Kula exchange that set the model for long-term participant-observation fieldwork.

name: Structure and Function in Primitive Society
summary: Collected essays setting out structural-functionalism, including those on the mother's brother and on joking relationships.

name: Witchcraft, Oracles and Magic Among the Azande
summary: Shows Azande witchcraft beliefs as a coherent system for explaining misfortune, separating inborn witchcraft from learned sorcery.

name: The Nuer
summary: Describes the ecology and political institutions of the Nuer, a stateless people held together by a segmentary lineage system.

name: Political Systems of Highland Burma
summary: Shows Kachin communities oscillating between hierarchical gumsa and egalitarian gumlao forms, challenging the idea of stable equilibrium.

name: The Elementary Structures of Kinship
aliases: Elementary Structures of Kinship|Les Structures élémentaires de la parenté
summary: Founds alliance theory: the incest taboo forces groups to exchange women, through restricted or generalised exchange.
note: French original 1949; English translation 1969.

name: The Ritual Process
aliases: The Ritual Process: Structure and Anti-Structure
summary: Uses Ndembu ritual to develop liminality and communitas, the bond among equals in the in-between phase of ritual.

name: Les Rites de Passage
summary: Shows that ceremonies of life crises and transitions share three phases: separation, transition and incorporation.
note: French original 1909; English translation 1960.

name: The Interpretation of Cultures
summary: Essays presenting culture as webs of meaning read through thick description, including 'Religion as a Cultural System'.

name: American Kinship: A Cultural Account
summary: Analyses American kinship as a system of symbols resting on shared biogenetic substance and a code for conduct.

name: Purity and Danger
summary: Argues that ideas of pollution and taboo protect a society's system of classification; dirt is matter out of place.

name: Stone Age Economics
summary: Calls hunter-gatherers the original affluent society and classifies reciprocity as generalised, balanced or negative.

name: Man Makes Himself
summary: Presents prehistory as a series of revolutions, chiefly the Neolithic and Urban Revolutions, driven by technology and economy.

name: The Gift
aliases: Essai sur le don|The Gift: Forms and Functions of Exchange in Archaic Societies
summary: Argues that gifts in archaic societies carry obligations to give, to receive and to repay, forming total social facts.
note: French original 1925 (some books give 1924); English translation 1954.

name: The Elementary Forms of Religious Life
aliases: Elementary Forms|The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life|Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse
summary: Defines religion by the division of sacred and profane and studies Australian totemism as its elementary form.
note: French original 1912; English translation 1915.

name: The Todas
summary: Ethnography of the Todas of the Nilgiris, known for fraternal polyandry and buffalo dairy ritual, built on recorded genealogies.

name: Ethnic Groups and Boundaries
summary: Edited volume whose introduction argues that ethnic groups persist through boundaries kept up in interaction, not shared culture alone.

name: On the Origin of Species
summary: Sets out evolution by natural selection acting on heritable variation in the struggle for existence.
note: Alfred Russel Wallace reached the same idea independently; their joint papers were read in 1858.

name: Experiments on Plant Hybridization
summary: Reports pea-plant crosses showing that hereditary factors segregate and assort independently in fixed ratios.
note: Read in 1865 and published in 1866; rediscovered in 1900 by de Vries, Correns and Tschermak.

name: An Essay on the Principle of Population
aliases: Essay on the Principle of Population|Principle of Population
summary: Argues that population outruns food supply unless held back by positive checks such as famine and disease or by preventive checks.

name: The People of India
summary: Classifies India's population into seven racial types from anthropometry and links caste rank to race.

name: Caste in India
summary: Survey of the caste system that explains its origin partly through tribal ideas of mana and taboo.
note: Not Ghurye's Caste and Race in India (1932).

name: The Mundas and Their Country
summary: Ethnography of the Munda of Chotanagpur, covering their history, land system and social life.

name: A Philosophy for NEFA
summary: Sets out a policy for developing the tribes of NEFA along the lines of their own culture, avoiding both isolation and forced assimilation.
note: The 1959 second edition carries Nehru's foreword with the Tribal Panchsheel.

name: Caste and Race in India
summary: Sets out six features of caste and traces its origin to the Brahmins of the Indo-Gangetic plain.

name: The Sacred Complex in Hindu Gaya
summary: Study of the pilgrimage town of Gaya that introduces the sacred complex of sacred geography, performances and specialists.

name: Indian Village
summary: Monograph on Shamirpet near Hyderabad describing the village as a social system of castes, economy and ritual.
note: Not Village India (1955), edited by McKim Marriott.

name: Religion and Society Among the Coorgs of South India
aliases: Religion and Society Among the Coorgs
summary: Study of Coorg ritual and caste in which Srinivas first set out Sanskritisation.

name: Village India: Studies in the Little Community
summary: Edited volume of Indian village studies, including Marriott's essay on universalisation and parochialisation in Kishan Garhi.
note: Not S.C. Dube's Indian Village (1955).

name: Peasant Society and Culture
summary: Describes peasant culture as a little tradition linked to the great tradition of a wider civilisation.

name: Homo Hierarchicus
aliases: Homo Hierarchicus: The Caste System and Its Implications
summary: Explains the caste system as hierarchy based on the opposition of pure and impure, in which status encompasses power.
note: French original 1966; English translation 1970.

name: Tribe, Caste and Nation
summary: Study of political activity and change among the Konds and Oriyas of highland Odisha.

name: Kinship Organisation in India
summary: Compares kinship terms and marriage rules across India and divides them into northern, central, southern and eastern zones.

name: Tribes of India: The Struggle for Survival
summary: Surveys how land alienation, forest policy and development have pressed on India's tribes since independence.

name: Animism
summary: Tylor's theory that religion began as belief in spiritual beings, an idea drawn from dreams, trances and death.

name: Animatism
summary: Marett's term for belief in an impersonal supernatural power, such as mana, which he placed before animism.

name: Naturism
summary: Max Müller's theory that religion arose from awe of the forces of nature, personified through language as gods.

name: Mana
summary: Melanesian and Polynesian idea of an impersonal supernatural power that can reside in people and things.
note: Reported by R.H. Codrington in The Melanesians (1891); Marett built animatism on it.

name: Sympathetic magic
summary: Frazer's two kinds of magic: homeopathic, based on the law of similarity, and contagious, based on the law of contact.

name: Sacred and profane
summary: Durkheim's division of things into the sacred, set apart and forbidden, and the ordinary profane; religion unites believers around the sacred.

name: Rites de passage
summary: Ceremonies marking a change of status, passing through phases of separation, transition (liminal) and incorporation.

name: Liminality
summary: The in-between phase of a rite of passage, where initiates are betwixt and between and share communitas.
note: Van Gennep named the liminal phase; Turner developed it.

name: Revitalization movement
summary: A deliberate, organised effort by members of a society to build a more satisfying culture, as defined by Anthony F.C. Wallace.

name: Kula ring
summary: Trobriand ceremonial exchange in which shell necklaces (soulava) travel clockwise and armshells (mwali) anticlockwise between island partners.

name: Substantivism
summary: Polanyi's view that pre-market economies are embedded in social relations and run by reciprocity and redistribution; formalists apply market economics everywhere.

name: Band, tribe, chiefdom and state
summary: Service's evolutionary typology of political organisation by increasing scale, centralisation and inequality.

name: Exogamy and endogamy
summary: Rules requiring marriage outside one's own group (exogamy) or within it (endogamy); McLennan coined both terms in Primitive Marriage.

name: Classificatory kinship terminology
summary: Morgan's contrast between terms that group lineal and collateral kin under one word (classificatory) and terms that keep them apart (descriptive).

name: Alliance theory
summary: Treats kinship as built on marriage exchange between groups rather than on descent, against the descent theory of Radcliffe-Brown and Fortes.

name: Structuralism
summary: Lévi-Strauss's search for the universal, unconscious structures of the mind, often binary oppositions, beneath kinship, myth and classification.

name: Historical particularism
summary: Boas's approach that each culture is the product of its own particular history, to be studied in detail before any generalisation.
note: The name was given by Marvin Harris in 1968, not by Boas.

name: Cultural relativism
summary: The principle that a culture's beliefs and practices should be understood in its own terms, not judged by another culture's standards.
note: Rooted in Boas; the term and its fullest statement came later, notably from Melville Herskovits.

name: Superorganic
summary: Kroeber's view that culture is a level of reality above the individual and the organic, following its own patterns.
note: Herbert Spencer used the word earlier; Kroeber's 1917 essay gave it its anthropological sense.

name: Culture area
summary: A geographical region whose peoples share a common set of culture traits, spreading from a culture centre.
note: Otis T. Mason used the term first; Wissler developed it and Kroeber refined it.

name: Status and role
summary: Linton's distinction of status as a position in a social system and role as its behavioural side; status is either ascribed or achieved.

name: Basic personality structure
summary: Personality traits shared by a society's members, shaped by primary institutions such as child-rearing and projected into secondary institutions such as religion.
note: Developed jointly by Kardiner and Ralph Linton.

name: Modal personality
summary: The personality type found most often in a society, measured statistically, as Cora Du Bois found on Alor.

name: Functionalism
summary: Malinowski's theory that every element of culture works to satisfy basic biological needs and the derived needs they create.

name: Structural-functionalism
summary: Radcliffe-Brown's theory that institutions function to maintain the social structure, the network of relations between persons.
note: Radcliffe-Brown rejected Malinowski's needs-based functionalism.

name: Thick description
summary: Geertz's method of describing behaviour together with the layered meanings it carries for the people involved.
note: Geertz took the term from the philosopher Gilbert Ryle.

name: White's law of cultural evolution
aliases: White's law|energy theory of cultural evolution
summary: Culture evolves as the energy harnessed per person per year increases, or as the efficiency of the tools using it increases (C = E x T).

name: Multilinear evolution
summary: Steward's view that cultures in similar environments follow parallel paths of development, rather than one universal sequence.

name: Cultural ecology
summary: Steward's study of how a culture core of subsistence and economic arrangements adapts to its environment.

name: Neolithic Revolution
summary: Childe's term for the shift from food gathering to food production by farming and herding, leading to settled village life.
note: Childe paired it with the later Urban Revolution.

name: Cultural materialism
summary: Harris's research strategy that explains structure and superstructure by the infrastructure of production and reproduction.

name: Heliocentric theory
summary: British diffusionist view that civilisation arose once, in ancient Egypt, and spread across the world with sun-worshipping 'Children of the Sun'.
note: Developed with W.J. Perry.

name: Kulturkreis
summary: German-Austrian diffusionist theory that culture spread in complexes (culture circles) from a few centres, traced by criteria of form and quantity.
note: Term from Leo Frobenius; method set out by Fritz Graebner and extended by Wilhelm Schmidt.

name: Genealogical method
summary: Rivers's method of collecting full genealogies to trace kinship terms, marriage, descent and other social facts.

name: Emic and etic
summary: Emic accounts describe a culture in its members' own categories; etic accounts use the observer's external, comparative categories.
note: Coined by linguist Kenneth Pike from phonemic and phonetic; popularised by Marvin Harris.

name: Sapir-Whorf hypothesis
summary: The idea that the structure of a language shapes how its speakers perceive and think about the world.
note: Named after Sapir and his student Benjamin Lee Whorf; they never stated it jointly.

name: Hardy-Weinberg law
summary: In a large, randomly mating population free of mutation, migration, selection and drift, allele and genotype frequencies stay constant.
note: Stated independently by G.H. Hardy and Wilhelm Weinberg in 1908.

name: Synthetic theory of evolution
summary: Joins Darwinian selection with Mendelian and population genetics: evolution results from mutation, recombination, selection, drift and isolation.
note: Built by Dobzhansky, Mayr, Simpson, Julian Huxley and others.

name: Ramapithecus
summary: Miocene ape from the Siwalik hills once claimed as an early human ancestor; now grouped with Sivapithecus as a relative of the orangutan.

name: Great tradition and little tradition
summary: Redfield's contrast between the reflective, written culture of a civilisation's elite and the oral, local culture of village folk.

name: Universalisation and parochialisation
summary: Universalisation carries little-tradition elements up into the great tradition; parochialisation carries great-tradition elements down into local forms.

name: Sanskritisation
summary: The process by which a low caste or tribe adopts the customs, rituals and beliefs of a higher, often twice-born, caste to claim higher rank.
note: Srinivas first called it Brahminisation in his Coorg study.

name: Dominant caste
summary: A caste that holds numerical strength, economic and political power, and fairly high ritual rank in a village or region.

name: Westernisation
summary: Srinivas's term for the changes in Indian society and culture that came with British rule, in technology, institutions, ideology and values.

name: Tribe-caste continuum
summary: The view that tribe and caste are poles of one continuum, on which a group is placed by how directly its members hold land.
note: Surajit Sinha also developed the idea.

name: Hindu method of tribal absorption
summary: N.K. Bose's account of how tribes are drawn into Hindu society as castes while keeping many of their own customs.

name: Sacred complex
summary: Vidyarthi's framework for a pilgrimage centre as the union of sacred geography, sacred performances and sacred specialists.

name: Nature-Man-Spirit complex
summary: Vidyarthi's view, from his study of the Maler hill tribe, that nature, man and the spirit world form one interdependent whole.

name: Isolation policy
summary: Elwin's early proposal to shield tribes from outside exploitation in protected areas, criticised as keeping them in 'national parks'.
note: Elwin later moved towards integration in his NEFA work.

name: Tribal Panchsheel
summary: Nehru's five principles for tribal policy: growth on their own genius, respect for land and forest rights, own people trained, no over-administration, results judged by human character.
note: Set out in Nehru's foreword to Elwin's A Philosophy for NEFA.

name: Jajmani system
summary: Hereditary patron-client ties in which service castes serve landowning patrons (jajmans) for fixed shares of grain and other dues.
note: First described in detail by William Wiser in The Hindu Jajmani System (1936).

name: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
summary: Tribal groups marked by pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a stagnant or declining population; 75 are listed.
note: Called Primitive Tribal Groups until renamed in 2006.

name: Founding of the Asiatic Society
summary: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta, beginning systematic study of India's peoples, languages and antiquities.

name: Discovery of the Pallavaram handaxe
summary: Robert Bruce Foote found a Palaeolithic handaxe at Pallavaram near Madras, the first recognised Palaeolithic tool in India.

name: Excavation of Harappa
summary: Daya Ram Sahni began excavating Harappa, bringing the Indus (Harappan) Civilisation to light; R.D. Banerji found Mohenjo-daro soon after.

name: First Census of India
summary: The first census of British India, taken at different times in different regions, is dated 1872.
note: The first synchronous census was held in 1881.

name: Founding of the Anthropological Survey of India
summary: The Government of India set up the Anthropological Survey of India, with B.S. Guha as its first director.

name: UNESCO Statement on Race
summary: UNESCO's first statement on race declared humankind one species and proposed 'ethnic groups' in place of 'race' for human groups.
note: Ashley Montagu was its rapporteur; revised statements followed.

name: Discovery of the Neanderthal type specimen
summary: Quarrymen found the type fossil of Neanderthal man in the Feldhofer cave in the Neander valley near Düsseldorf, Germany.
note: Earlier finds at Engis (1829) and Gibraltar (1848) were recognised as Neanderthal only later.

name: Discovery of Java Man
summary: Eugène Dubois found a skullcap at Trinil on the Solo river in Java, the first fossil now classed as Homo erectus.
note: Dubois named it Pithecanthropus erectus in 1894.

name: Discovery of Lucy
summary: Donald Johanson's team found the partial skeleton of a female Australopithecus afarensis at Hadar in Ethiopia.
note: The species Australopithecus afarensis was named in 1978.

name: Discovery of Narmada Man
summary: Arun Sonakia of the Geological Survey of India found a hominin skull cap at Hathnora in the Narmada valley, the first hominin fossil from India.
note: Sonakia classed it as Homo erectus; later studies treat it as archaic Homo sapiens.

name: Dhebar Commission
aliases: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes Commission|U.N. Dhebar Commission
summary: Commission under U.N. Dhebar that reviewed Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes and found wide inequality among tribes.

name: Lokur Committee
summary: Committee that set five criteria for listing Scheduled Tribes: primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.

name: Mandal Commission
summary: Commission under B.P. Mandal that identified Other Backward Classes and recommended 27 per cent reservation for them in central government jobs.
note: Set up in 1979 and reported in 1980; implementation was announced in 1990.

name: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act
summary: Extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas and gives gram sabhas powers over land, minor forest produce and local resources.
note: Based on the Bhuria Committee's recommendations.

name: Forest Rights Act
aliases: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act|FRA
summary: Recognises individual and community rights of Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers over forest land and resources.
note: Passed in 2006; in force from 31 December 2007.

name: Xaxa Committee
aliases: High Level Committee on tribal communities
summary: High-level committee under Virginius Xaxa that reported on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities.
note: Set up in 2013; reported in 2014.

name: Santhal rebellion
summary: Rising of the Santhals of the Rajmahal hills under Sidhu and Kanhu against zamindars, moneylenders and colonial officials.
